sentences.zh: =李揆=李揆字端卿，隴西成紀人，而家於鄭州，代為冠族。

translations.literal: Li Kui, styled Duanching, was a native of Longxi Chenji but his family resided in Zhengzhou; for generations they were a leading clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui, whose courtesy name was Duanching, came from Longxi Chenji but his family had long lived in Zhengzhou, where for generations they ranked among the foremost great houses.

sentences.zh: 秦府學士、給事中玄道玄孫，秘書監、贈吏部尚書成裕之子。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Xuandao, a scholar of the Prince of Qin's household and a superviser-remonstrator; and the son of Chengyu, Director of the Secretariat and posthumously Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from Xuandao, who had served as a scholar in the Prince of Qin's household and as a superviser-remonstrator, and was the son of Chengyu, Director of the Secretariat, who was posthumously made Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and fond of learning, and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was quick-witted and devoted to study, and he excelled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 開元末，舉進士，補陳留尉，獻書闕下，詔中書試文章，擢拜右拾遺。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Chenliu district defender, presented a memorial at the palace gates; on imperial order the Secretariat tested his literary compositions and he was promoted to Right Remonstrance-reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Kaiyuan reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed defender of Chenliu. After he submitted a book to the court, the emperor ordered the Secretariat to examine his writings and promoted him to Right Remonstrance-reminder.

sentences.zh: 改右補闕、起居郎，知宗子表疏。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Supplementation-reminder and Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and was charged with imperial-clan memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Right Supplementation-reminder and Attendant of the Heir Apparent, with responsibility for memorials from members of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 遷司勛員外郎、考功郎中，並知制誥。

translations.literal: He was promoted to outer office director in the Ministry of Personnel and bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, and in both posts drafted imperial rescripts.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to outer office director in the Ministry of Personnel and bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, serving in both offices as a drafter of imperial rescripts.

sentences.zh: 扈從劍南，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor to Jiannan and was appointed Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When the court went to Jiannan he accompanied it and was appointed a drafter of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，兼禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyuan era he also served as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyuan era he was additionally appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 揆嘗以主司取士，多不考實，徒峻其堤防，索其書策，殊未知藝不至者，文史之囿亦不能摛詞，深昧求賢之意也。

translations.literal: Kui once observed that chief examiners in selecting scholars often did not verify true ability but merely heightened barriers and demanded written answers, wholly failing to see that those without talent could not compose even within the bounds of letters and histories—profoundly missing the intent of seeking the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Kui had long felt that chief examiners, in selecting candidates, seldom tested real ability. They only raised barriers and demanded written answers, never recognizing that men without talent could not compose even within the familiar fields of letters and history. In this they utterly missed the purpose of seeking worthy men.

sentences.zh: 其試進士文章，請於庭中設《五經》、諸史及《切韻》本於床，而引貢士謂之曰：「大國選士，但務得者，經籍在此，請恣尋檢。

translations.literal: For the jinshi literary examination he requested that copies of the Five Classics, various histories, and the Qieyun be set on couches in the courtyard, and led the candidates in, saying: "A great state selects scholars only to obtain the able; the classics are here—please search and consult as you wish."
translations.idiomatic: For the jinshi literary examination he had copies of the Five Classics, the standard histories, and the Qieyun placed on couches in the courtyard. He then brought the candidates before him and said, "A great state chooses its scholars only to find the able. The books are here—consult them freely."

sentences.zh: 」由是數月之間，美聲上聞，未及畢事，遷中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿崇文館大學士、修國史。

translations.literal: " Within a few months his fine reputation reached the throne; before the examination was finished he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, Grand Academician of the Jixian and Chongwen halls, and compiler of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: " Within a few months his reputation for fairness reached the emperor. Before the examination cycle was even finished, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, Grand Academician of the Jixian and Chongwen halls, and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 揆美風儀，善奏對，每有敷陳，皆符獻替。

translations.literal: Kui had a fine bearing and was skilled in memorial replies; whenever he set forth proposals they accorded with the principle of offering and replacing.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was distinguished in bearing and skilled in audience with the throne. Whatever he proposed was apt counsel, offered to improve and replace what was amiss.

sentences.zh: 肅宗賞嘆之，嘗謂揆曰：「卿門地、人物、文章，皆當代所推。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong admired him and once said to Kui: "Your lineage, person, and writings are all praised in our age."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong admired him greatly and once told Kui, "Your family standing, your person, and your writings are all esteemed in our time."

sentences.zh: 」故進人稱為三絕。

translations.literal: " Hence people at court called him the three incomparables.
translations.idiomatic: " For this reason contemporaries called him unmatched in three respects.

sentences.zh: 其為舍人也，宗室請加張皇后「翊聖」之號，肅宗召揆問之，對曰；

translations.literal: While he was a Secretariat drafter, members of the imperial clan asked to add the title "Assistant Sage" to Empress Zhang; Emperor Suzong summoned Kui and questioned him, and he replied:
translations.idiomatic: While he served as a Secretariat drafter, members of the imperial clan petitioned to add the honorific "Assistant Sage" to Empress Zhang. Emperor Suzong summoned Kui for his view, and he answered:

sentences.zh: 「臣觀往古后妃，終則有謚。

translations.literal: "Your servant observes that empresses and consorts of old received posthumous titles only at the end.
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant observes that in antiquity empresses and consorts received posthumous titles only after death.

sentences.zh: 生加尊號，未之前聞。

translations.literal: To add an honorific title during life has never been heard of before.
translations.idiomatic: To bestow a grand honorific title during one's lifetime is without precedent.

sentences.zh: 景龍失政，韋氏專恣，加號翊聖，今若加皇后之號，與韋氏同。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era government failed, the Wei clan acted willfully, and the title Assistant Sage was added; if Your Majesty now adds such a title to the empress, it will be the same as with the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong era the court lost its way, the Wei clan seized power, and the title Assistant Sage was added. If Your Majesty now adds such a title to the empress, you will be repeating the Wei precedent.

sentences.zh: 陛下明聖，動遵典禮，豈可蹤景龍故事哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty is enlightened and sage and always follows the canonical rites—how could you follow the Jinglong precedent!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is enlightened and always observant of ritual—how could you follow the Jinglong precedent!

sentences.zh: 」肅宗驚曰：「凡才幾誤我家事。

translations.literal: " Emperor Suzong was startled and said: "Mediocre talent nearly ruined my household affairs."
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Suzong was startled and said, "Mediocre counsel nearly ruined my house."

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: " The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was then abandoned.

sentences.zh: 時代宗自廣平王改封成王，張皇后有子數歲，陰有奪宗之議。

translations.literal: At that time Daizong had been changed from Prince of Guangping to Prince of Cheng; Empress Zhang had a son several years old, and secretly there was talk of displacing the heir.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Daizong had been renamed from Prince of Guangping to Prince of Cheng. Empress Zhang had a young son, and there was secret talk of displacing the heir.

sentences.zh: 揆因對見，肅宗從容曰：「成王嫡長有功，今當命嗣，卿意何如？

translations.literal: When Kui came to audience, Emperor Suzong said calmly: "The Prince of Cheng is the eldest legitimate son and has merit; he should now be named heir—what is your view?"
translations.idiomatic: On one audience Kui was present, and Emperor Suzong said calmly, "The Prince of Cheng is the eldest legitimate son and has rendered service. It is time to name the heir. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」揆拜賀曰：「陛下言及於此，社稷之福，天下幸甚，臣不勝大慶。

translations.literal: " Kui bowed in congratulation and said: "That Your Majesty speaks of this is the fortune of the altars of soil and grain and great happiness for the realm; your servant cannot contain his great joy."
translations.idiomatic: " Kui bowed in congratulation and said, "That Your Majesty speaks of this is a blessing to the altars of state and a great fortune for the realm. Your servant is overcome with joy."

sentences.zh: 」肅宗喜曰：「朕計決矣。

translations.literal: " Emperor Suzong said with pleasure: "My decision is made."
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Suzong said gladly, "My mind is made up."

sentences.zh: 」自此頗承恩遇，遂蒙大用。

translations.literal: " From then on he received considerable imperial favor and came to great employment.
translations.idiomatic: " From that time he enjoyed marked imperial favor and was soon entrusted with great power.

sentences.zh: 時京師多盜賊，有通衢殺人置溝中者，李輔國方恣橫，上請選羽林騎士五百人以備巡檢。

translations.literal: At that time the capital had many bandits; some killed people on main roads and cast the bodies into ditches. Li Fuguo was then acting with unchecked arrogance and requested that five hundred Imperial Guard horsemen be selected for patrol inspection.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits were numerous in the capital; murders on busy streets and bodies thrown into ditches were common. Li Fuguo, then riding high in power, asked that five hundred Imperial Guard horsemen be chosen for patrol duty.

sentences.zh: 揆上疏曰：「昔西漢以南北軍相攝，故周勃因南軍入北軍，遂安劉氏。

translations.literal: Kui submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly in Western Han the Southern and Northern Armies kept each other in check; therefore Zhou Bo entered the Northern Army through the Southern Army and thus secured the Liu house."
translations.idiomatic: Kui submitted a memorial saying, "In Western Han the Southern and Northern Armies were meant to check each other. That was why Zhou Bo, by way of the Southern Army, entered the Northern Army and thereby secured the Liu house."

sentences.zh: 皇朝置南北衙，文武區分，以相伺察。

translations.literal: Our dynasty established the Northern and Southern Bureaus, separating civil and military, so that each might watch the other.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty established the Northern and Southern Bureaus, separating civil and military authority so that each might watch the other.

sentences.zh: 今以羽林代金吾警夜，忽有非常之變，將何以制之？

translations.literal: Now to have the Imperial Guard replace the Golden Crow for night watch—if a sudden extraordinary change occurs, how will it be controlled?
translations.idiomatic: If the Imperial Guard now replaces the Golden Crow in night patrol, and a sudden crisis arises, how will it be controlled?

sentences.zh: 」遂制罷羽林之請。

translations.literal: " The request for Imperial Guard forces was then ordered withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: " The request for Imperial Guard patrols was then ordered withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 揆在相位，決事獻替，雖甚博辨，性銳於名利，深為物議所非。

translations.literal: While Kui was in the chief ministership he decided affairs with corrective counsel and was very eloquent in debate, but by nature he was keen for fame and profit and was deeply criticized in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister Kui decided affairs with apt corrective counsel and was highly eloquent, yet he was keen for fame and profit and was widely condemned.

sentences.zh: 又其兄皆自有時名，滯於冗官，竟不引進。

translations.literal: Moreover his elder brothers all had reputations in their time but were stuck in superfluous posts; he never advanced them.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brothers, too, enjoyed reputations of their own but languished in minor posts, and he never advanced them.

sentences.zh: 同列呂諲，地望雖懸，政事在揆之右，罷相，自賓客為荊南節度，聲問甚美。

translations.literal: His colleague Lü Yin, though far below him in lineage and standing, had been his superior in government; dismissed from the chief ministership, he went from guest to military commissioner of Jingnan, and his reputation was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: His colleague Lü Yin, though far beneath him in birth and standing, had once outranked him in government. After leaving the chief ministership Lü went from imperial guest to military commissioner of Jingnan, where his reputation flourished.

sentences.zh: 懼其重入，遂密令直省至諲管內抅求諲過失。

translations.literal: Fearing his return to office, Kui secretly ordered direct secretariat officials to go into Yin's jurisdiction and seek out Yin's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Yin might return to high office, Kui secretly ordered secretariat officials to enter Yin's jurisdiction and hunt for faults.

sentences.zh: 諲密疏自陳，乃貶揆萊州長史同正員，其制旨曰：「扇湖南之八州，沮江陵之節制。

translations.literal: Yin submitted a secret memorial in his own defense, and Kui was demoted to senior administrator of Laizhou with concurrent regular status; the edict said: "He stirred up the eight prefectures south of the lake and obstructed control from Jiangling."
translations.idiomatic: Yin submitted a secret memorial in his own defense, and Kui was demoted to senior administrator of Laizhou. The edict declared, "He stirred up the eight prefectures south of the lake and obstructed control from Jiangling."

sentences.zh: 」揆既黜官，數日，其兄皆改授為司門員外郎。

translations.literal: " After Kui was removed from office, within a few days his brothers were all reassigned as outer office directors in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: " Within days of Kui's dismissal his brothers were all reassigned to outer office director posts in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 後累年，揆量移歙州刺史。

translations.literal: After several years Kui was transferred by quota to prefect of Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: After several years Kui was transferred by quota to prefect of Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 初，揆秉政，侍中苗晉卿累薦元載為重官。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Kui held power, Palace Attendant Miao Jinqing repeatedly recommended Yuan Zai for a weighty post.
translations.idiomatic: While Kui held power, Palace Attendant Miao Jinqing had repeatedly recommended Yuan Zai for high office.

sentences.zh: 揆自恃門望，以載地寒，意甚輕易，不納，而謂晉卿曰：「龍章鳳姿之士不見用，麞頭鼠目之子乃求官。

translations.literal: Kui relied on his lineage and, because Zai's background was humble, treated him very lightly and would not accept him, saying to Jinqing: "Men of dragon markings and phoenix bearing go unused, while deer-headed, rat-eyed fellows seek office."
translations.idiomatic: Kui, trusting in his own pedigree, looked down on Zai because of his humble origins and refused the recommendation. He told Jinqing, "Men of dragon markings and phoenix bearing go unused, while deer-headed, rat-eyed fellows come seeking office."

sentences.zh: 」載銜恨頗深。

translations.literal: " Zai bore a very deep grudge.
translations.idiomatic: " Zai nursed a deep grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 及載登相位，因揆當徙職，遂奏為試秘書監，江淮養疾。

translations.literal: When Zai reached the chief ministership, taking advantage of Kui's due transfer, he memorialized that Kui be made acting Director of the Secretariat to convalesce in Jianghuai.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai became chief minister, he took advantage of Kui's scheduled transfer and had him appointed acting Director of the Secretariat to convalesce in the Jianghuai region.

sentences.zh: 既無祿俸，家復貧乏，孀孤百口，丐食取給。

translations.literal: He had no salary, his household was again impoverished, and a hundred widows and orphans begged for food to survive.
translations.idiomatic: With no salary and his household again in want, more than a hundred widows and orphans in his family lived by begging.

sentences.zh: 萍寄諸州，凡十五六年，其牧守稍薄，則又移居，故其遷徙者，蓋十余州焉。

translations.literal: He drifted like duckweed among the prefectures for fifteen or sixteen years in all; if a prefect was somewhat harsh he moved again, so the places to which he shifted numbered more than ten prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: For fifteen or sixteen years he drifted from prefecture to prefecture. Whenever a local governor treated him harshly he moved on again, and in all he lived in more than ten different prefectures.

sentences.zh: 元載以罪誅，除揆睦州刺史，入拜國子祭酒、禮部尚書，為盧杞所惡。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai was executed for crime, Kui was appointed prefect of Muzhou; he entered court as Director of the Directorate of Education and Minister of Rites, but was hated by Lu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Zai was executed for his crimes, Kui was appointed prefect of Muzhou. He later entered court as Director of the Directorate of Education and Minister of Rites, but Lu Qi bore him ill will.

sentences.zh: 德宗在山南，令充入蕃會盟使，加左僕射。

translations.literal: When Dezong was in Shannan he was ordered to serve as envoy to the western tribes for the alliance conference and was given the additional title of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While Dezong was in Shannan, Kui was appointed envoy to the western tribes for the alliance conference and was additionally made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 行至鳳州，以疾卒，興元元年四月也，年七十四。

translations.literal: Reaching Fengzhou he died of illness, in the fourth month of the first year of Xingyuan; he was seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Fengzhou and died of illness in the fourth month of the first year of Xingyuan, at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，喪事官給。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, and his funeral expenses were supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, and the state provided for his funeral.

sentences.zh: =李涵=李涵，高平王道立曾孫。

translations.literal: Li Han was the great-grandson of Daoli, Prince of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han was the great-grandson of Daoli, Prince of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 父少康，宋州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Shaokang was prefect of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaokang had served as prefect of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 涵簡素恭慎，有名宗室，累授贊善大夫、兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Han was plain, frugal, respectful, and cautious, a noted member of the imperial clan, and was repeatedly appointed gentleman attendant and concurrent palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: Han was plain, frugal, respectful, and cautious, a well-known member of the imperial clan who was repeatedly appointed gentleman attendant and concurrent palace censor.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度郭子儀奏為關內鹽池判官。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi, military commissioner of Shuofang, memorialized that he be made salt-pond administrator within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, military commissioner of Shuofang, recommended him as salt-pond administrator for the region within the passes.

sentences.zh: 肅宗北幸平涼，未有所適。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong went north to Pingliang and had not yet decided where to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong went north to Pingliang, the court had not yet chosen its next refuge.

sentences.zh: 涵與朔方留後杜鴻漸，草箋具朔方兵馬招集之勢，軍資倉儲庫物之數，鹹推涵宗枝之英，純厚忠信，乃令涵奉箋至平涼謁見。

translations.literal: Han and Du Hongjian, acting commissioner of Shuofang, drafted a memorial setting forth the strength of Shuofang troops being gathered, and the numbers of military supplies, granaries, and storehouses; all praised Han as an outstanding branch of the imperial clan, pure, generous, loyal, and trustworthy, and so Han was ordered to present the memorial at Pingliang for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Du Hongjian, acting commissioner of Shuofang, drafted a memorial detailing the forces being gathered in Shuofang and the quantities of military supplies in store. All praised Han as an outstanding member of the imperial clan, pure, generous, loyal, and trustworthy, and Han was sent to present the memorial at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 涵敷奏明辯，動合事機，肅宗大悅，除右司員外郎，累至司封郎中、宗正少卿。

translations.literal: Han presented his case clearly and persuasively, and his words always matched the moment; Emperor Suzong was greatly pleased and appointed him outer office director in the Right Secretariat, and he rose in time to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites and Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Han spoke clearly and persuasively, and his words always matched the moment. Emperor Suzong was greatly pleased and appointed him outer office director in the Right Secretariat. He later rose to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites and Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，初平河朔，代宗以涵忠謹洽聞，遷左庶子、兼御史中丞、河北宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, when the Hebei region was first pacified, Daizong, because Han was known for loyalty, prudence, and thoroughness, promoted him to Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, concurrent Censor-in-chief, and Hebei pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying, when the Hebei region was first pacified, Daizong promoted Han—known for loyalty, prudence, and thoroughness—to Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with concurrent appointment as Censor-in-chief and Hebei pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會丁母憂，起復本官而行，每州縣郵驛，公事之外，未嘗啟口，疏飯飲水，席地而息。

translations.literal: He happened to enter mourning for his mother but was recalled to his former post and set out; at every postal station in prefecture and county, apart from official business he never opened his mouth, ate plain food and drank water, and slept on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He was in mourning for his mother but was recalled to his former post and set out. At every postal station along the way, apart from official business he scarcely spoke, ate plain food and drank water, and slept on the ground.

sentences.zh: 使還，請罷官終喪制，代宗以其毀瘠，許之。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he asked to leave office and complete the mourning period; Daizong, seeing how emaciated he was from grief, granted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission ended he asked to leave office and complete his mourning. Daizong, seeing how grief had wasted him, granted the request.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除給事中，遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Supervising Secretary and promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed Supervising Secretary and later promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以幽州之亂，充河朔宣慰使。

translations.literal: Because of the turmoil in Youzhou he was made Hebei-Shuo pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the turmoil in Youzhou he was appointed Hebei-Shuo pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大歷六年正月，為蘇州刺史、兼御史大夫，充浙江西道都團練觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year of Dali he became prefect of Suzhou, concurrent Chief Censor, and overall training-and-defense and observation commissioner of western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year of Dali he was made prefect of Suzhou, concurrent Chief Censor, and overall training-and-defense and observation commissioner of western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十一年，來朝，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he came to court and was appointed Chief Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he came to court and was appointed Chief Censor.

sentences.zh: 京畿觀察使李棲筠歿，代之。

translations.literal: When Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of the capital region, died, Han replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of the capital region, died, Han succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，以涵和易，無剸割之才，除太子少傅，充山陵副使。

translations.literal: When Dezong took the throne, because Han was easygoing and lacked the talent for sharp cutting decisions, he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and deputy commissioner for the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong took the throne, judging Han easygoing and lacking the talent for decisive action, he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and deputy commissioner for the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 涵判官殿中侍御史呂渭上言：「涵父名少康，今官名犯諱，恐乖禮典。

translations.literal: Han's aide, Palace Attendant-in-chief Lü Wei, submitted a statement: "Han's father's name is Shaokang; his present official title violates taboo and may conflict with ritual canon."
translations.idiomatic: Han's aide, Palace Attendant-in-chief Lü Wei, submitted a statement: "Han's father's name is Shaokang. His present official title violates taboo and may conflict with ritual propriety."

sentences.zh: 」宰相崔祐甫奏曰：「若朝廷事有乖舛，群臣悉能如此，實太平之道。

translations.literal: " Chief Minister Cui Youfu memorialized: "If whenever court affairs go astray all ministers can act thus, that is truly the way of great peace."
translations.idiomatic: " Chief Minister Cui Youfu memorialized, "If whenever court affairs go astray all ministers can speak up like this, that is truly the way to great peace."

sentences.zh: 」除渭司門員外郎。

translations.literal: " Wei was appointed outer office director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei was appointed outer office director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 尋有人言：「涵昔為宗正少卿，此時無言，今為少傅，妄有奏議。

translations.literal: Soon someone said: "When Han was formerly Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court he said nothing; now as Junior Tutor he presumptuously submitted this opinion."
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone objected: "When Han was Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court he said nothing about this; now, as Junior Tutor, his aide presumptuously submitted this opinion."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「呂渭僭陳章奏，為其本使薄訴官名。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Lü Wei presumptuously submitted a memorial, making a petty complaint about an official title on behalf of his chief."
translations.idiomatic: " An edict declared, "Lü Wei presumptuously submitted a memorial, making a petty complaint about an official title on behalf of his chief."

sentences.zh: 朕以宋有司城之嫌，晉有詞曹之諱，嘆其忠於所事，亦謂確以上聞。

translations.literal: We recalled that in Song there was the taboo of the Minister of Works and in Jin the taboo of the Bureau of Documents, admired his loyalty to his charge, and also thought he had been earnest in reporting upward.
translations.idiomatic: We recalled that in Song there was the taboo involving the Minister of Works and in Jin the taboo involving the Bureau of Documents. We admired his loyalty to his chief and thought he had been earnest in reporting upward.

sentences.zh: 乃加殊恩，俾膺厚賞。

translations.literal: We therefore granted him special favor and allowed him a generous reward.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore granted him special favor and a generous reward.

sentences.zh: 近聞所陳「少」字，往歲已任少卿，昔是今非，罔我何甚！

translations.literal: We have lately heard that the character "shao" of which he complained—years ago Han already held the post of Vice Director; what was acceptable then is unacceptable now—how greatly he has deceived Us!
translations.idiomatic: We have lately learned that the character shao in question was no issue when Han already held the post of Vice Director years ago. What was acceptable then is unacceptable now—how greatly he has deceived Us!

sentences.zh: 豈得謬當朝典，更廁周行，宜佐遐籓，用誡薄俗。

translations.literal: How can he wrongly hold a court norm and again stand in the imperial ranks? He should assist a distant frontier prefecture to warn shallow custom.
translations.idiomatic: How can he wrongly hold a post at court and again stand among the imperial ranks? He should serve in a distant frontier prefecture as a warning to shallow custom.

sentences.zh: 可歙州司馬同正。

translations.literal: He is fit to be vice prefect of Shezhou with concurrent regular status.
translations.idiomatic: He is demoted to vice prefect of Shezhou with concurrent regular status.

sentences.zh: 」由是改涵為檢校工部尚書、兼光祿卿，仍充山陵副使。

translations.literal: " Han was therefore changed to acting Minister of Public Works and concurrent Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, while still serving as deputy commissioner for the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: " Han was therefore reassigned as acting Minister of Public Works and concurrent Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, while retaining his post as deputy commissioner for the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 無幾，以右僕射致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he retired as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 興元元年九月卒，追贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He died in the ninth month of the first year of Xingyuan and was posthumously made Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of the first year of Xingyuan and was posthumously made Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: =陳少遊=陳少遊，博州人也。

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou was a native of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou was a native of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 祖儼，安西副都護。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan was Vice Protector-general of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan had served as Vice Protector-general of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 父慶，右武衛兵曹參軍，以少遊累贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Qing was a military staff officer of the Right Martial Guards; because of Shaoyou he was repeatedly posthumously made Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qing had been a military staff officer of the Right Martial Guards; because of Shaoyou he was repeatedly posthumously made Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 少遊幼聰辯，初習《莊》、《列》、《老子》，為崇玄館學生，眾推引講經。

translations.literal: Shaoyou was clever and eloquent in youth; he first studied the Zhuangzi, Liezi, and Laozi, became a student of the Chongxuan Hall, and the crowd recommended him to expound the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou was clever and eloquent as a youth. He first studied the Zhuangzi, Liezi, and Laozi, entered the Chongxuan Hall as a student, and his fellows recommended him to lecture on the classics.

sentences.zh: 時同列有私習經義者，期升坐日相問難。

translations.literal: At that time some of his fellows had privately studied the meaning of the classics and set a day when they would ascend the seat and question one another.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his fellows had privately studied the classics and arranged to question one another on the day he took the lectern.

sentences.zh: 及會，少遊攝齊升坐，音韻清辯，觀者屬目。

translations.literal: When the meeting came, Shaoyou gathered his robes and ascended the seat; his tones were clear and his argument keen, and the onlookers fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came, Shaoyou gathered his robes and ascended the seat. His voice was clear and his argument keen, and every eye in the hall was on him.

sentences.zh: 所引文句，悉兼他義，諸生不能對，甚為大學士陳希烈所嘆賞，又以同宗，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: The passages he cited all carried additional meanings; the students could not reply, and Grand Academician Chen Xilie greatly admired him; moreover, being of the same clan, he treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Every passage he cited carried additional meanings, and the students could not answer him. Grand Academician Chen Xilie greatly admired him, and because they shared the same surname clan, treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 既擢第，補渝州南平令，理甚有聲。

translations.literal: After he passed the examination he was appointed magistrate of Nanping in Yuzhou, and his governance won great renown.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the examination he was appointed magistrate of Nanping in Yuzhou, where his governance won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 至德中，河東節度王思禮奏為參謀，累授大理司直、監察殿中侍御史、節度判官。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era Wang Silu, military commissioner of Hedong, memorialized that he be made staff adviser; he was repeatedly appointed rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review, investigating palace censor, and military commissioner aide.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhide era Wang Silu, military commissioner of Hedong, recommended him as staff adviser. He rose through appointments as rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review, investigating palace censor, and military commissioner aide.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，入為金部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying he entered court as outer office director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying he entered court as outer office director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋授侍御史、迥紇糧料使，改檢校職方員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was made attendant censor and grain-supply commissioner for the Uyghurs, and was changed to acting outer office director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made attendant censor and grain-supply commissioner for the Uyghurs, and was reassigned as acting outer office director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 充使檢校郎官，自少遊始也。

translations.literal: Serving as envoy with acting courtier rank began with Shaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of appointing an envoy with acting courtier rank began with Shaoyou.

sentences.zh: 明年，仆固懷恩奏為河北副元帥判官、兵部郎中、兼侍御史。

translations.literal: The next year Pugu Huai'en memorialized that he be made aide to the deputy commander-in-chief of Hebei, bureau director in the Ministry of War, and concurrent attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Pugu Huai'en recommended him as aide to the deputy commander-in-chief of Hebei, bureau director in the Ministry of War, and concurrent attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 遷晉州刺史，改同州刺史，未視事，又歷晉、鄭二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Jinzhou, then changed to prefect of Tongzhou; before taking office he again served as prefect of Jin and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Jinzhou, then reassigned to Tongzhou. Before he could take up that post he served again as prefect of Jin and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 少遊為理，長於權變，時推幹濟，然厚斂財貨，交結權幸，以是頻獲遷擢。

translations.literal: Shaoyou in governing was skilled in expedient adaptation; his contemporaries praised his practical ability, yet he heavily levied wealth and cultivated connections with the powerful and favored, and thereby frequently gained promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In governing, Shaoyou was skilled at expedient adaptation and was praised for practical ability. Yet he levied heavy taxes, cultivated the powerful and favored at court, and thereby won frequent promotion.

sentences.zh: 無幾，澤潞節度使李抱玉表為副使、御史中丞、陳鄭二州留後。

translations.literal: Before long Li Baoyu, military commissioner of Zelu, memorialized that he be made deputy commissioner, Censor-in-chief, and acting governor of Chen and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Baoyu, military commissioner of Zelu, recommended him as deputy commissioner, Censor-in-chief, and acting governor of Chen and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 永泰二年，抱玉又奏為隴右行軍司馬，拜檢校左庶子，依前兼中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongtai Baoyu again memorialized that he be made marching army vice marshal of Longyou, appointed acting Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and as before concurrently Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongtai Baoyu again recommended him as marching army vice marshal of Longyou and acting Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, while retaining his concurrent post as Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 其年，除桂州刺史、桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed prefect of Guizhou and observation commissioner of the Gui circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was appointed prefect of Guizhou and observation commissioner of the Gui circuit.

sentences.zh: 少遊以嶺僥遐遠，欲規求近郡。

translations.literal: Shaoyou, because the Ling region was remote and perilous, wished to scheme for a nearer prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou, finding the Ling region remote and arduous, set about securing a post nearer the capital.

sentences.zh: 時中官董秀掌樞密用事，少遊乃宿於其裏，候其下直，際晚謁之，從容曰：「七郎家中人數幾何？

translations.literal: At that time the eunuch Dong Xiu controlled secret affairs and wielded power; Shaoyou lodged in his lane, waited until he left duty, and at dusk called on him, saying calmly: "Seventh Brother, how many people are in your household?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time the eunuch Dong Xiu controlled secret affairs and wielded great power. Shaoyou lodged in his lane, waited until he left duty, and at dusk called on him. Calmly he asked, "Seventh Brother, how large is your household?"

sentences.zh: 每月所費復幾何？

translations.literal: How much do you spend each month?
translations.idiomatic: And how much do you spend each month?

sentences.zh: 」秀曰：「久忝近職，家累甚重，又屬時物騰貴，一月過千餘貫。

translations.literal: " Xiu said: "Having long held a post near the throne, my household burdens are very heavy, and as prices are rising, a month costs more than a thousand strings of cash."
translations.idiomatic: " Xiu replied, "Having long held a post near the throne, my household burdens are heavy. With prices rising as they are, a month costs more than a thousand strings of cash."

sentences.zh: 」少遊曰：「據此之費，俸錢不足支數日，其餘常須數求外人，方可取濟。

translations.literal: " Shaoyou said: "By this reckoning your salary would not last a few days; the rest must constantly be sought from outsiders before you can make ends meet."
translations.idiomatic: " Shaoyou said, "At that rate your salary would not last a few days. The rest must constantly be sought from outsiders before you can make ends meet."

sentences.zh: 倘有輸誠供億者，但留心庇覆之，固易為力耳。

translations.literal: If someone offers sincere support in supplying your needs, you need only take care to shelter him—it is easy enough to manage.
translations.idiomatic: If someone offers you sincere support, you need only take him under your protection—it is easily done.

sentences.zh: 少遊雖不才，請以一身獨供七郎之費，每歲請獻錢五萬貫。

translations.literal: Though I am without talent, I ask to supply Seventh Brother's expenses alone myself, offering fifty thousand strings of cash each year.
translations.idiomatic: Though I lack talent, I ask to supply all of Seventh Brother's expenses myself, offering fifty thousand strings of cash each year.

sentences.zh: 今見有大半，請即受納，餘到官續送。

translations.literal: I now have more than half on hand—please accept it at once; the rest I will continue sending once I take office.
translations.idiomatic: I have more than half of it on hand now—please accept it at once. The rest I will send once I take up my post.

sentences.zh: 免貴人勞慮，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: Would it not spare a nobleman's anxieties?
translations.idiomatic: Would that not spare you worry?

sentences.zh: 」秀既逾於始望，欣愜頗甚，因與之厚相結。

translations.literal: " Xiu, exceeding his first hopes, was greatly pleased and formed a close bond with him.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiu, far beyond what he had first hoped for, was greatly pleased and formed a close bond with him.

sentences.zh: 少遊言訖，泣曰：「南方炎瘴，深愴違辭，但恐不生還再睹顏色矣。

translations.literal: When Shaoyou finished speaking he wept and said: "The southern heat and miasma deeply grieve me at parting; I fear I shall not return alive to see your face again."
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyou had finished he wept and said, "The southern heat and miasma grieve me deeply at this parting. I fear I shall not return alive to see you again."

sentences.zh: 」秀遽曰：「中丞美才，不當遠官，請從容旬日，冀竭蹇分。

translations.literal: " Xiu said hastily: "Vice Censor, your talent is too fine for a distant post. Please allow ten days or so; I hope to do my poor utmost."
translations.idiomatic: " Xiu said hastily, "Vice Censor, your talent is too fine for a distant post. Give me ten days or so; I hope to do what little I can."

sentences.zh: 」時少遊又已納賄於元載子仲武矣。

translations.literal: " At that time Shaoyou had also paid bribes to Yuan Zai's son Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: " By then Shaoyou had also paid bribes to Yuan Zai's son Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 秀、載內外引薦，數日，拜宣州刺史、宣歙池都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: Xiu and Zai recommended him inside and outside court; within a few days he was appointed prefect of Xuanzhou and overall training-and-defense and observation commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi.
translations.idiomatic: With recommendations from Xiu within the palace and Zai outside it, within a few days he was appointed prefect of Xuanzhou and overall training-and-defense and observation commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi.

sentences.zh: 大歷五年，改越州刺史、兼御史大夫、浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dali he was changed to prefect of Yuezhou, concurrent Chief Censor, and observation commissioner of eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dali he was reassigned as prefect of Yuezhou, concurrent Chief Censor, and observation commissioner of eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 八年遷揚州大都督府長史、淮南節度觀察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to senior administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture and military commissioner and observation commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made senior administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture and military commissioner and observation commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 仍加銀青光祿大夫，封潁川縣開國子。

translations.literal: He was additionally given the Silver-Green Glory Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Viscount of Yingchuan county.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made Silver-Green Glory Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Viscount of Yingchuan county.

sentences.zh: 所在悉心綏輯，而多以任數為政，好行小惠，胥吏得職，人亦獲安。

translations.literal: Wherever he was he devoted himself to pacification and ordering, yet he often governed by expedient stratagems, liked to grant small favors, clerks fulfilled their duties, and the people also found security.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he devoted himself to pacifying and ordering the region, yet he often governed by expedient stratagems and liked to grant small favors. Clerks fulfilled their duties and the people found a measure of security.

sentences.zh: 及朝廷多事。

translations.literal: When the court had many affairs,
translations.idiomatic: When the court was beset by many crises,

sentences.zh: 奏請本道兩稅錢千增二百。

translations.literal: he memorialized that the circuit's two-tax cash be increased by two hundred per thousand.
translations.idiomatic: he memorialized that the circuit's two-tax payments be increased by two hundred cash per thousand.

sentences.zh: 因詔諸道悉如淮南，鹽每一斗更加一百文。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon ordered all circuits to follow Huainan, adding one hundred cash to each dou of salt.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered every circuit to follow Huainan's example, adding one hundred cash to the price of each dou of salt.

sentences.zh: 少遊十餘年間，三總大籓，皆天下殷厚處也。

translations.literal: Within a dozen years Shaoyou thrice headed great frontier commands, all in the wealthiest parts of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than a decade Shaoyou thrice headed great frontier commands, each in one of the wealthiest regions of the empire.

sentences.zh: 以故征求貿易，且無虛日，斂積財寶，累巨億萬，多賂遺權貴，視文雅清流之士，蔑如也。

translations.literal: Therefore levies and trade went on without a single idle day; he amassed treasure amounting to hundreds of millions, gave many bribes to the powerful and favored, and looked with contempt on refined and upright scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Levies and trade went on without a single idle day. He amassed wealth in the hundreds of millions, lavished bribes on the powerful and favored at court, and held refined scholars in contempt.

sentences.zh: 初結元載，每年饋金帛約十萬貫，又多納賂於用事中官駱奉先、劉清潭、吳承倩等，由是美聲達於中禁。

translations.literal: At first he cultivated Yuan Zai, sending him gold and silk worth about a hundred thousand strings each year, and also paid many bribes to influential eunuchs such as Luo Fengxian, Liu Qingtan, and Wu Chengqian; thereby his good reputation reached the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: At first he cultivated Yuan Zai, sending him gifts of gold and silk worth about a hundred thousand strings each year. He also paid many bribes to influential eunuchs such as Luo Fengxian, Liu Qingtan, and Wu Chengqian, and his reputation for generosity reached the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 後見元載在相位年深，以過犯漸見疑忌，少遊亦稍疏之。

translations.literal: Later, seeing that Yuan Zai had long been chief minister and was gradually suspected because of faults, Shaoyou also grew somewhat distant from him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, seeing that Yuan Zai had long held the chief ministership and was gradually falling under suspicion for his faults, Shaoyou also grew somewhat distant from him.

sentences.zh: 無何，載子伯和貶官揚州，少遊外與之交結，而陰使人伺其過失，密以上聞。

translations.literal: Before long Zai's son Bohe was demoted to an office in Yangzhou; Shaoyou outwardly cultivated friendship with him while secretly sending men to watch for his faults and reporting them in secret to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zai's son Bohe was demoted to an office in Yangzhou. Shaoyou cultivated him outwardly while secretly sending men to watch for his faults and reporting them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 代宗以為忠，待之益厚。

translations.literal: Daizong regarded this as loyalty and treated him all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong regarded this as loyalty and treated him all the more generously.

sentences.zh: 上即位，累加檢校禮部、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne he was repeatedly given acting appointments as Minister of Rites and Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong took the throne, Shaoyou was repeatedly given acting appointments as Minister of Rites and Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，李納反叛，少遊以師收徐、海等州，尋棄之，退軍盱眙。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong Li Na rebelled; Shaoyou with his army recovered Xu, Hai, and other prefectures, then soon abandoned them and withdrew his army to Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianzhong Li Na rebelled. Shaoyou recovered Xu, Hai, and other prefectures with his army, then soon abandoned them and withdrew to Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 又加檢校左僕射，賜實封三百戶。

translations.literal: He was additionally made acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and granted three hundred actual fief households.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and granted three hundred actual fief households.

sentences.zh: 其年，就加同平章事。

translations.literal: That year he was given the additional title of Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was given the additional title of Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 關播嘗為少遊賓僚，盧杞早年與之同在仆固懷恩使府，故驟加其官秩。

translations.literal: Guan Bo had once been Shaoyou's guest official, and Lu Qi had early been with him in Pugu Huai'en's mission office; therefore his rank was suddenly raised.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo had once served on Shaoyou's staff, and Lu Qi had been with him early in Pugu Huai'en's mission office; for these reasons his rank was suddenly raised.

sentences.zh: 四年十月，駕幸奉天，度支汴東兩稅使包佶在揚州，尚未知也。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year the emperor went to Fengtian; Bao Ji, commissioner of the eastern Bian two-tax revenues in the Ministry of Revenue, was in Yangzhou and did not yet know of it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year the emperor fled to Fengtian. Bao Ji, commissioner of the eastern Bian two-tax revenues, was in Yangzhou and had not yet heard the news.

sentences.zh: 佶判官崔沅遽報少遊，佶時所總賦稅錢帛約八百萬貫在焉，少遊意以為賊據京師，未即收復，遂脅取其財物。

translations.literal: Ji's aide Cui Yuan hastily reported to Shaoyou; the tax revenues in cash and silk under Ji's control amounted to about eight million strings; Shaoyou supposed the rebels held the capital and it would not soon be recovered, and so coerced seizure of the goods.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's aide Cui Yuan hastily reported to Shaoyou. The tax revenues under Ji's control amounted to about eight million strings of cash. Shaoyou supposed the rebels held the capital and it would not soon be recovered, and so seized the goods by force.

sentences.zh: 先使判官崔就佶強索其納給文歷，並請供二百萬貫錢物以助軍費，佶答曰：「所用財帛，須承敕命。

translations.literal: He first sent his aide Cui to Ji to demand forcibly his delivery records, and also requested two million strings of cash and goods to aid military expenses; Ji replied: "Funds and goods used must await imperial order."
translations.idiomatic: He first sent his aide Cui to demand Ji's delivery records by force and also requested two million strings of cash and goods for military expenses. Ji replied, "Funds and goods may be used only on imperial order."

sentences.zh: 」未與之。

translations.literal: " He would not give them.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused.

sentences.zh: 勃然曰：「中丞若得，為劉長卿；

translations.literal: Shaoyou said angrily: "Vice Censor, if you comply, you will be like Liu Changqing;
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou said angrily, "Vice Censor, if you comply, you will fare like Liu Changqing;

sentences.zh: 不爾，為崔眾矣。

translations.literal: if not, you will be like Cui Zhong."
translations.idiomatic: if not, you will fare like Cui Zhong."

sentences.zh: 」長卿嘗任租庸使，為吳仲孺所困，崔眾供軍吝財，為光弼所殺，故言及之，佶大懼，不敢固護，財帛將轉輸入京師者，悉為少遊奪之。

translations.literal: " Liu Changqing had once served as transport commissioner and was trapped by Wu Zhongru; Cui Zhong was stingy in supplying the army and was killed by Guangbi—hence he mentioned them. Ji was greatly afraid and did not dare firmly defend the goods; all the funds and goods about to be transported to the capital were seized by Shaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Changqing had once served as transport commissioner and was trapped by Wu Zhongru; Cui Zhong had been stingy in supplying the army and was killed by Li Guangbi—hence the threat. Ji was terrified and did not dare resist. All the funds and goods destined for the capital were seized by Shaoyou.

sentences.zh: 佶自謁，少遊止焉，長揖而遣，既懼禍，奔往白沙。

translations.literal: Ji came in person to call; Shaoyou detained him, bowed deeply and sent him off; fearing disaster, Ji fled to Baisha.
translations.idiomatic: Ji came in person to call on him. Shaoyou detained him, bowed deeply, and sent him away. Fearing for his life, Ji fled to Baisha.

sentences.zh: 少遊又遣判官房孺復召之，佶愈懼，托以巡檢，因急棹過江，妻子伏案牘中。

translations.literal: Shaoyou again sent his aide Fang Rufu to summon him; Ji grew still more afraid, pleaded an inspection tour, and hurriedly rowed across the river, his wife and children hiding among the documents.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou again sent his aide Fang Rufu to summon him. Ji grew still more afraid, pleaded an inspection tour, and hurriedly crossed the river by boat, his wife and children hiding among the document cases.

sentences.zh: 至上元，復為韓滉所拘留。

translations.literal: Reaching Shangyuan he was again detained by Han Huang.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Shangyuan he was again detained by Han Huang.

sentences.zh: 佶先有兵三千，守禦財貨，令高越、元甫將焉，少遊盡奪之。

translations.literal: Ji had formerly had three thousand troops guarding the goods, commanded by Gao Yue and Yuan Fu; Shaoyou seized them all.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had formerly had three thousand troops guarding the goods under Gao Yue and Yuan Fu; Shaoyou seized them all.

sentences.zh: 隨佶渡江者，又為韓滉所留，佶但領胥吏往江、鄂等州。

translations.literal: Those who crossed the river with Ji were again detained by Han Huang; Ji led only clerks on to Jiang, E, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had crossed the river with Ji were again detained by Han Huang. Ji went on to Jiang, E, and other prefectures with only a few clerks.

sentences.zh: 佶於彈丸中置表，以少遊脅取財帛事。

translations.literal: Ji placed a memorial inside a pellet ball reporting Shaoyou's coercion of funds and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Ji placed a memorial inside a pellet ball reporting Shaoyou's seizure of the funds and goods.

sentences.zh: 會少遊使繼至，上問曰：「少遊取包佶財帛，有之乎？

translations.literal: When Shaoyou's envoy arrived in succession, the emperor asked: "Did Shaoyou take Bao Ji's funds and goods?"
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyou's envoy arrived, the emperor asked, "Did Shaoyou take Bao Ji's funds and goods?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣發揚州後，非所知也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "After your servant left Yangzhou, I do not know."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "After I left Yangzhou, I do not know."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「少遊國之守臣，或防他盜，供費軍旅，收亦何傷。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Shaoyou is a guardian minister of the state; he may guard against other robbers and supply military expenses—what harm in taking them?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Shaoyou is a guardian minister of the state. He may need to guard against other robbers and supply the army—what harm is there in taking them?"

sentences.zh: 」時方隅阻絕，國命未振，遠近聞之大驚，鹹以聖情達於變通，明見萬里。

translations.literal: " At that time the regions were cut off and the nation's mandate was not yet restored; near and far heard this and were greatly startled, all thinking the sage heart understood expedient adaptation and saw clearly for ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: " The regions were cut off and the dynasty's authority was not yet restored. Near and far, all who heard this were astonished, and took it as proof that the emperor understood expedient adaptation and saw clearly across the realm.

sentences.zh: 少遊後聞之，乃安。

translations.literal: When Shaoyou later heard of it he was reassured.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyou later heard of it he was reassured.

sentences.zh: 及李希烈陷汴州，聲言欲襲江淮。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie captured Bianzhou he declared he would attack Jianghuai.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie captured Bianzhou he declared his intention to strike at Jianghuai.

sentences.zh: 少遊懼，乃使參謀溫述由壽州送款於希烈曰：「濠、壽、舒、廬，尋令罷壘，韜戈卷甲，佇候指揮。

translations.literal: Shaoyou was afraid and sent his staff adviser Wen Shu from Shouzhou with submission to Xilie, saying: "Hao, Shou, Shu, and Lu—I shall soon order the forts dismantled, sheathe swords and roll up armor, and await your command."
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou was afraid and sent his staff adviser Wen Shu from Shouzhou to submit to Xilie, saying, "For Hao, Shou, Shu, and Lu—I shall soon order the forts dismantled, sheathe our swords and roll up our armor, and await your command."

sentences.zh: 」少遊又遣巡官趙詵於鄆州結李納。

translations.literal: " Shaoyou also sent touring official Zhao Shen to Yanzhou to ally with Li Na.
translations.idiomatic: " Shaoyou also sent touring official Zhao Shen to Yanzhou to ally with Li Na.

sentences.zh: 其年，希烈僭號，遣其將楊豐賫偽赦書赴揚州，至壽州，為刺史張建封候騎所得，建封對中使二人及少遊判官許子瑞廷責豐而斬之。

translations.literal: That year Xilie usurped the title of emperor and sent his general Yang Feng bearing a false amnesty to Yangzhou; reaching Shouzhou he was seized by scouting horsemen of Prefect Zhang Jianfeng, who in court before two palace envoys and Shaoyou's aide Xu Zirui rebuked Feng and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xilie declared himself emperor and sent his general Yang Feng with a false amnesty to Yangzhou. At Shouzhou he was seized by Zhang Jianfeng's scouts. Zhang rebuked Feng in open court before two palace envoys and Shaoyou's aide Xu Zirui, then beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 希烈聞之大怒，即署其大將杜少誠為偽僕射、淮南節度，令先平壽州，後取廣陵。

translations.literal: Xilie heard this and was greatly enraged; he immediately appointed his great general Du Shaoqian false Vice Director and Huainan military commissioner, ordering him first to pacify Shouzhou and then take Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie was enraged and immediately appointed his great general Du Shaoqian false Vice Director and Huainan military commissioner, ordering him first to pacify Shouzhou and then take Guangling.

sentences.zh: 建封於霍丘堅柵，嚴加守禁，少誠竟不能進。

translations.literal: Jianfeng built strong palisades at Huoqiu and strictly guarded them; Shaoqian in the end could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng built strong palisades at Huoqiu and guarded them strictly; Shaoqian could not advance.

sentences.zh: 後包佶入朝，具奏少遊奪財賦事狀，少遊大懼，乃上表，以所取包佶財貨，皆是供軍急用，今請據數卻納。

translations.literal: Later Bao Ji entered court and fully reported Shaoyou's seizure of revenues; Shaoyou was greatly afraid and submitted a memorial saying the goods taken from Bao Ji had all been urgently needed for the army and that he now asked to return them according to the amount.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bao Ji came to court and fully reported Shaoyou's seizure of the revenues. Shaoyou was terrified and submitted a memorial claiming that what he had taken from Bao Ji had all been urgently needed for the army and offering to return the full amount.

sentences.zh: 既而州府殘破，無以上填，乃與腹心孔目官等設法重稅管內百姓以供之。

translations.literal: The prefecture and offices were then ravaged and there was no way to make repayment; he therefore with trusted clerks devised heavy taxes on the people within his jurisdiction to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was ravaged and there was no way to make repayment. He therefore worked with trusted clerks to levy heavy taxes on the people under his jurisdiction to supply it.

sentences.zh: 無何，劉洽收汴州，得希烈偽起居註「某月日陳少遊上表歸順。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Qia recovered Bianzhou and obtained Xilie's false attendance diary: "On such-and-such a day Chen Shaoyou submitted a memorial of submission."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liu Qia recovered Bianzhou and obtained Xilie's false attendance diary, which recorded that on a certain day Chen Shaoyou had submitted a memorial of submission.

sentences.zh: 」少遊聞之，慚惶發疾，數日而卒，年六十一，贈太尉，賻布帛，葬祭如常儀。

translations.literal: " When Shaoyou heard of it he was ashamed and fearful, fell ill, and died within a few days at the age of sixty-one; he was posthumously made Grand Commandant, given funeral silks, and buried with the usual rites.
translations.idiomatic: " When Shaoyou heard of it he was overcome with shame and fear, fell ill, and died within a few days at the age of sixty-one. He was posthumously made Grand Commandant, given funeral silks, and buried with the usual rites.

sentences.zh: =盧鸑=盧鸑，幽州范陽人也，貞觀中工部侍郎義恭玄孫也。

translations.literal: Lu Bie was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou and the great-great-grandson of Yigong, Vice Minister of Public Works in the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bie was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou and the great-great-grandson of Yigong, who had served as Vice Minister of Public Works in the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 父子騫，潁王府諮議參軍，以鸑贈秘書少監。

translations.literal: His father Ziqian was advisory staff officer of the Prince of Ying's household; because of Bie he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ziqian had been advisory staff officer of the Prince of Ying's household; because of Bie he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 鸑少以門廕入仕，在職以幹局稱。

translations.literal: Bie early entered office through yin privilege and in service was known for practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: Bie entered office early through yin privilege and was known in service for practical ability.

sentences.zh: 累授閬州錄事參軍、監察殿中御史、侍御史、金州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed records officer of Langzhou, investigating palace censor, attendant censor, and prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through appointments as records officer of Langzhou, investigating palace censor, attendant censor, and prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 宰相楊炎遇之頗厚，召入左司郎中、京兆少尹，遷大尹。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Yang Yan treated him very generously, summoned him in as bureau director in the Left Secretariat and junior magistrate of the capital district, and promoted him to chief magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Yang Yan treated him generously, brought him to court as bureau director in the Left Secretariat and junior magistrate of the capital district, and then promoted him to chief magistrate.

sentences.zh: 鸑無術學，善事權要，為政苛躁。

translations.literal: Bie had no learning in the arts, was skilled at serving the powerful and favored, and in governing was harsh and rash.
translations.idiomatic: Bie had no scholarly training, was skilled at cultivating the powerful and favored, and governed harshly and rashly.

sentences.zh: 盧杞甚惡之，諷有司彈奏，坐貶撫州司馬同正，改饒州刺史，遷福州刺史、福建觀察使。

translations.literal: Lu Qi greatly hated him, hinted that the relevant offices impeach him, and he was demoted to vice prefect of Fuzhou with concurrent regular status, then changed to prefect of Raozhou and transferred to prefect of Fuzhou and observation commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi hated him and prompted the relevant offices to impeach him. He was demoted to vice prefect of Fuzhou, then reassigned as prefect of Raozhou, and later transferred to prefect of Fuzhou and observation commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年七月，以疾終。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Zhenyuan he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Zhenyuan he died of illness.

sentences.zh: =裴谞=裴谞，字士明，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Pei Xu, styled Shiming, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xu, whose courtesy name was Shiming, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父寬，禮部尚書，有重名於開元、天寶間。

translations.literal: His father Kuan was Minister of Rites and had a great reputation in the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuan had served as Minister of Rites and enjoyed a great reputation in the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras.

sentences.zh: 谞少舉明經，補河南府參軍，通達簡率，不好苛細。

translations.literal: Xu early passed the mingjing examination, was appointed staff officer of Henan prefecture, was open and straightforward, and disliked petty exactness.
translations.idiomatic: Xu passed the mingjing examination in youth and was appointed staff officer of Henan prefecture. He was open and straightforward and disliked petty exactness.

sentences.zh: 積官至京兆倉曹，丁父喪，居東都。

translations.literal: He rose in office to granary officer of the capital district, entered mourning for his father, and resided in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to granary officer of the capital district, then entered mourning for his father and resided in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 是時，安祿山盜陷二京，東都收復，遷太子司議郎。

translations.literal: At that time An Lushan rebelled and seized the two capitals; when the eastern capital was recovered he was transferred to Master of Petitions of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time An Lushan rebelled and seized the two capitals. When the eastern capital was recovered, Xu was made Master of Petitions of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 無幾，虢王巨奏署侍御史、襄鄧營田判官，丁母憂。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince of Guo, Ju, memorialized his appointment as attendant censor and agricultural colony aide of Xiang and Deng, and he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Prince of Guo recommended him as attendant censor and agricultural colony aide of Xiang and Deng. He then entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 東都復為史思明所陷，谞藏匿山谷。

translations.literal: The eastern capital was again seized by Shi Siming, and Xu hid in the mountains and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern capital fell again to Shi Siming, and Xu hid in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 思明嘗為谞父將校，懷舊恩，又素慕谞名，欲必得之，因令捕騎數十跡逐得谞。

translations.literal: Siming had once been a commander under Xu's father and cherished the old kindness; he had also long admired Xu's name and was determined to have him, so he sent several dozen pursuit horsemen who tracked him down and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Siming had once served under Xu's father and cherished the old bond. He had also long admired Xu's reputation and was determined to have him. He sent several dozen horsemen in pursuit, who tracked Xu down and captured him.

sentences.zh: 思明見之，甚喜，呼為郎君，不名，偽授御史中丞，主擊斷。

translations.literal: When Siming saw him he was greatly pleased, called him Young Master without using his name, and falsely appointed him Censor-in-chief in charge of judgments.
translations.idiomatic: When Siming saw him he was greatly pleased, addressed him as Young Master without using his personal name, and falsely appointed him Censor-in-chief in charge of judgments.

sentences.zh: 時思明殘殺宗室，谞陰緩之，全活者數百人。

translations.literal: At that time Siming slaughtered members of the imperial clan; Xu secretly slowed the process, and several hundred were preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Siming was slaughtering members of the imperial clan. Xu secretly slowed the process, and several hundred lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 又嘗疏賊短長以聞，事泄，思明大怒詬罵，僅而免死。

translations.literal: He also once memorialized the rebels' strengths and weaknesses to inform the court; when the matter leaked out Siming was furious and reviled him, and he barely escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: He also once sent a memorial reporting the rebels' strengths and weaknesses to the court. When the matter leaked, Siming was furious and reviled him, and he barely escaped death.

sentences.zh: 賊平，除太子中允，遷考功郎中，數召見言事。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was appointed Palace Companion of the Heir Apparent, promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, and repeatedly summoned to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were pacified he was appointed Palace Companion of the Heir Apparent and promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites. He was repeatedly summoned to speak on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 代宗居陜，谞步懷考功及南曹二印赴行在，上見而謂之曰：「疾風知勁草，果信矣。

translations.literal: When Daizong was in Shan, Xu walked carrying the seals of the Ministry of Rites and the Southern Bureau to the mobile court; the emperor saw him and said: "The fierce wind reveals the tough grass—how true indeed."
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong was in Shan, Xu walked to the mobile court carrying the seals of the Ministry of Rites and the Southern Bureau. The emperor saw him and said, "The fierce wind reveals the tough grass—how true that saying is."

sentences.zh: 」將以為御史中丞，為無載所排，為河東道租庸鹽鐵等使。

translations.literal: " He was about to be made Censor-in-chief but was blocked by Yuan Zai and instead became commissioner of transport, salt, and iron for the Hedong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " He was about to be made Censor-in-chief but was blocked by Yuan Zai and was instead appointed commissioner of transport, salt, and iron for the Hedong circuit.

sentences.zh: 時關輔大旱，谞入計，代宗召見便殿，問谞：「榷酤之利，一歲出入幾何？

translations.literal: At that time the capital region suffered great drought; Xu came to present accounts, and Daizong summoned him to the side hall and asked: "What are the yearly receipts and expenditures of the monopoly on wine?"
translations.idiomatic: The capital region was suffering a great drought. Xu came to present accounts, and Daizong summoned him to the side hall and asked, "What are the yearly receipts and expenditures of the wine monopoly?"

sentences.zh: 」谞久之不對。

translations.literal: " Xu for a long time did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu was silent for a long time.

sentences.zh: 上復問之，對曰：「臣有所思。

translations.literal: The emperor asked again, and he replied: "Your servant has something on his mind."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again, and he replied, "Your servant has something on his mind."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「何思？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "What is on your mind?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "What is it?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣自河東來，其間所歷三百里，見農人愁嘆，谷菽未種。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Coming from Hedong, over three hundred li that I passed I saw farmers grieving and sighing, grain and beans not yet sown."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Coming from Hedong, over the three hundred li I traveled I saw farmers grieving. Grain and beans had not yet been sown."

sentences.zh: 誠謂陛下軫念，先問人之疾苦，而乃責臣以利。

translations.literal: I truly thought Your Majesty would be concerned and first ask about the people's suffering, yet you press your servant about profit.
translations.idiomatic: I truly thought Your Majesty would be concerned and first ask about the people's suffering, yet you press me about profit.

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：理國者，仁義而已，何以利為？

translations.literal: Mencius said: He who governs a state needs only benevolence and righteousness—why speak of profit?
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said that governing a state requires only benevolence and righteousness—why speak of profit?

sentences.zh: 由是未敢即對也。

translations.literal: For this reason I did not dare answer at once.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason I did not dare answer at once.

sentences.zh: 」上前坐曰：「微公言，吾不聞此。

translations.literal: " The emperor came forward and sat, saying: "But for your words I would not have heard this."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor came forward and sat down. "But for your words," he said, "I would not have heard this."

sentences.zh: 」拜左司郎中。

translations.literal: " He was appointed bureau director in the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed bureau director in the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上時訪以事，執政者忌之，出為虔州刺史，歷饒、廬、亳三州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor often consulted him on affairs; those in power envied him and he was sent out as prefect of Qianzhou, then served as prefect of Rao, Lu, and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often consulted him on affairs of state. Those in power envied him, and he was sent out as prefect of Qianzhou, then served as prefect of Rao, Lu, and Bo.

sentences.zh: 入為右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court as general of the Right Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered court as general of the Right Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 建中初，上以刑名理天下，百吏震悚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong the emperor governed the realm by penal law; all officials were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong era the emperor governed the realm through penal law, and all officials were shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 時十月禁屠殺，以甫近山陵，禁益嚴。

translations.literal: At that time slaughter was forbidden in the tenth month because the imperial tombs were near, and the prohibition was especially strict.
translations.idiomatic: At that time slaughter was forbidden in the tenth month because the imperial tombs were near, and the prohibition was especially strict.

sentences.zh: 尚父、汾陽王郭子儀隸人殺羊以入，門者覺之，谞列奏狀，上以為不畏強禦，累遣宣諭。

translations.literal: The Meritous Father, Prince of Fenyang Guo Ziyi, had a servant kill a sheep and bring it in; the gate guards detected it, and Xu submitted a detailed memorial; the emperor thought he did not fear the powerful and repeatedly sent imperial commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The Meritous Father, Prince of Fenyang Guo Ziyi, had a servant kill a sheep and bring it in. The gate guards detected it, and Xu submitted a detailed memorial. The emperor thought he did not fear the powerful and repeatedly sent imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 或謂谞曰：「郭公有社稷功，豈不為蓋之？

translations.literal: Someone said to Xu: "The Prince has merit to the altars of state—would you not cover for him?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Xu, "The Prince has rendered great service to the state—would you not cover for him?"

sentences.zh: 」谞笑曰：「非爾所解。

translations.literal: " Xu smiled and said: "That is not something you would understand."
translations.idiomatic: " Xu smiled and said, "That is not something you would understand."

sentences.zh: 且郭公威權太盛，上新即位，必謂黨附者眾。

translations.literal: Moreover the Prince's authority is too great; the emperor has newly taken the throne and is sure to think his faction numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Prince's authority is too great. The emperor has newly taken the throne and is sure to think his faction numerous.

sentences.zh: 今發其細過，以明不弄權耳。

translations.literal: By exposing a small fault now, I make clear that he does not manipulate power.
translations.idiomatic: By exposing a small fault now, I make clear that he does not manipulate power.

sentences.zh: 吾上以盡事君之道，下以安大臣，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: Above I thereby fulfill the way of serving one's lord; below I thereby reassure a great minister—is that not fitting?
translations.idiomatic: In doing so I fulfill my duty to the throne above and reassure a great minister below—is that not fitting?

sentences.zh: 」時於朝堂別置三司以決庶獄，辯爭者輒擊登聞鼓，谞上疏曰：「夫諫豉謗木之設，所以達幽枉，延直言。

translations.literal: " At that time three offices were separately set up in the court hall to decide common cases; disputants would strike the Audience Drum, and Xu submitted a memorial saying: "The remonstrance drum and the slander post were established to reach hidden wrongs and draw forth straight speech."
translations.idiomatic: " At that time three offices were separately established in the court hall to decide common cases, and disputants would strike the Audience Drum. Xu submitted a memorial saying, "The remonstrance drum and the slander post were established to reach hidden wrongs and draw forth straight speech."

sentences.zh: 今輕猾之人，援桴鳴鼓，始動天聽，竟因纖微。

translations.literal: Now frivolous and cunning men take the mallet and strike the drum, first moving the heavenly ear, yet in the end it is over trifles.
translations.idiomatic: Now frivolous and cunning men strike the drum and reach the emperor's ear, yet in the end their cases turn on trifles.

sentences.zh: 若然者，安用吏理乎！

translations.literal: If it is thus, what need is there for officials to govern?
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, what need is there for officials to govern?

sentences.zh: 」上然之，悉歸有司。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved and returned all cases to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved and returned all such cases to the regular offices.

sentences.zh: 谞以法吏舞文，多挾宿怨，因獻《獄官箴》以諷。

translations.literal: Xu, because legal clerks twisted the written law and often bore old grudges, presented the Admonition for Prison Officials as a satire.
translations.idiomatic: Because legal clerks twisted the written law and often bore old grudges, Xu presented the Admonition for Prison Officials as an indirect remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 無何，坐所善僧抵法，貶閬州司馬。

translations.literal: Before long, because a monk he favored violated the law, he was demoted to vice prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, because a monk he favored violated the law, he was demoted to vice prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 征為右庶子，改千牛上將軍。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent and changed to senior general of the Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent and reassigned as senior general of the Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃入寇，尋拜吏部侍郎、兼御史大夫，為吐蕃使，不行。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans invaded he was soon appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrent Chief Censor, and was made envoy to the Tibetans but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans invaded he was soon appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrent Chief Censor, and was named envoy to Tibet but did not go.

sentences.zh: 無幾，轉太子賓客、兵部侍郎、河南尹、東都副留守。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Guest of the Heir Apparent, Vice Minister of War, magistrate of Henan, and deputy protector of the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Guest of the Heir Apparent, Vice Minister of War, magistrate of Henan, and deputy protector of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 谞自河南凡五代為官，入視事，未嘗當正處，不鞫認於贓罪，以寬厚和易為理。

translations.literal: From Henan through five reigns in office, whenever Xu entered to conduct affairs he never sat in the main seat, did not press confessions in cases of embezzlement, and governed with generous forbearance and easy mildness.
translations.idiomatic: Through five reigns in office from Henan onward, whenever Xu took up his duties he never sat in the main seat, did not press confessions in embezzlement cases, and governed with generous forbearance and easy mildness.

sentences.zh: 貞元九年十一月，以疾終，年七十五，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year of Zhenyuan he died of illness at the age of seventy-five and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the ninth year of Zhenyuan he died of illness at the age of seventy-five and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: =【贊】=史臣曰：李揆發言沃心，幸遇明主；

translations.literal: The historian says: Li Kui's words enriched the heart and he was fortunate to meet an enlightened lord;
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Li Kui's words enriched the sovereign's heart, and he was fortunate to meet an enlightened ruler;

sentences.zh: 蔽賢固位，終非令人。

translations.literal: yet in screening out the worthy and holding fast to his post he was in the end not a man to be admired.
translations.idiomatic: yet in screening out the worthy and clinging to his post he was not, in the end, a man to be admired.

sentences.zh: 少遊逐勢利隨時，盧惎事權要巧宦，察言觀行，皆無可稱。

translations.literal: Shaoyou chased profit and power as times shifted; Lu Qi served the powerful and favored as a crafty office-seeker—in examining words and observing conduct, none is praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou chased profit and power as the times shifted; Lu Qi cultivated the powerful and favored as a crafty office-seeker—in examining their words and conduct, none is praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 涵節行著聞，谞和易為理，庶幾近仁也。

translations.literal: Han's conduct was renowned, and Xu governed with easy mildness—they come close to benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Han's conduct was renowned, and Xu governed with easy mildness—they come close to true benevolence.

sentences.zh: 贊曰李、陳、盧鸑，言行非真。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Li, Chen, and Lu Bie—their words and conduct were not genuine.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Li, Chen, and Lu Bie—their words and conduct were not genuine.

sentences.zh: 涵、谞和易，庶乎近仁。

translations.literal: Han and Xu, easy and mild—they come close to benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Xu, easy and mild in manner—they come close to benevolence.
